newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker very quiet, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker very quiet, rates steady.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the Middle East Gulf was very slow on Thursday, with rates holding firm on the previous day's levels, shipping brokers said.
Other lifting sectors saw unchanged freight rates.

Although no VLCC or ULCC fixtures were done brokers said rates to Japan held around W65 while tankers bound for the U.S and Europe were still assessed around W55. VLCCs travelling for Singapore and Taiwan were estimated to be in the W60-62 region.
Although chartering in the Mediterranean was poor rates were unmoved. 80,000 tonners going cross-Med were put at a steady W100-103.
In the inter-UKC rates on 80,000 tonners were steady around W100, although up to W105 was done, with Total seen taking Fosna from Tees to Immingham. No transatlantic charters were seen.

The Caribbean saw rates settle around last done levels, U.S. brokers said. It was estimated that 70,000 tonners travelling Caribs up the U.S coast were steady at W130. Hunt Petroleum took the Kentucky from Mexico at W135.
West African rates consolidated themselves amid slightly slower chartering to the U.S and Asia. Rates for Suezmaxes to the U.S were placed in a range of W86-88.
